C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

phases.name: Traceability
phases.goal: Keep user-facing guide claims, architecture boundaries, implementation, and verification visibly connected.
phases.exit: Every traceability row names its requirement, guide and architecture sections, implementation files, verification command, receipt or refusal, owner, and status.

items.title: Generate holistic feature traceability and architecture conformance
items.what: Provide a reusable Python engine that reads project-owned reviewed manifests, scans every configured repository, validates stable requirement, workflow-node, code-anchor, test-case, test-report and issue references, compares the expected workflow graph with the actual implementation graph, and generates an overall dashboard plus per-feature drill-down without AI-authored runtime state.
items.done: The reusable command validates reviewed mappings across configured repository checkouts, resolves stable symbol/region/file and test-case anchors, verifies revision-bound test reports, classifies expected-versus-actual workflow coverage, generates a responsive overall and per-feature page, and fails check mode on stale output or broken evidence without AI runtime calls.

log.event: Sponsor directed Common Rules implementation with an overall view first, feature-by-feature expected-versus-actual architecture conformance, typed code references, test-case IDs and visible test reports.
log.evidence: Sponsor conversation 2026-10-03; Docs accepted visual proposal revision 6

asks.quote: So could you implement this as part of the common rules, a set of Python scripts that you can trigger and then create this traceability based on the criteria you have given?
Could it be made somewhat common, or would it be project-specific?

And you have for test sets well you have something like test cases or something like that, for test report and for implementation. It's pointing to something like for each layer. Is it something visible?

Can we actually have some references? Like requirement has some actual reference code IDs, and those references are written in code, start and end and something like that, or we refer a complete file. Test case can be test IDs.
Implement the script, but my aim is I want AI to first. How much time will it take for AI to complete the traceability?

So my aim is we pick up each feature at a time and we make sure the code is also architected accordingly. Can we look at it in a holistic view? Is it possible that bean is architected in the same way the workflow is expected to run?
merge it to main and make a release
